the rat's medial prefrontal area contains neurons that respond to sucrose solution intake and that the neurons can be classified into two groups, anticipatory and consummatory, according to their response characteristics.
the rat's prefrontcortical activity is modulated by sucrose consumption.
neuronal activity changes of the rat medial prefrontcortex were observed during sucrose solution licking, and the changes were time locked to the first lick of licking cluster.

the neuronal activity in medial prefrontal cortical neurons in rats during sucrose solution drinking.
the neuronal activity of rat medial prefrontcortex during sucrose solution licking.
the role of the prefrontal cortex in the control of ingestive behavior.

the medial prefrontcortex is involved in the integration of feeding-related sensory information and in the anticipation of liquid food reward.
the medial prefrontcortex is involved in the processing and integration of feeding-related sensory information.
the medial prefrontcortical neurons respond to both the anticipation and consummations of sucrose solution.

the prefrontal cortex is involved in the integration of the information of the reward and its consumption, as well as the integration of the reward information with the internal and external environment.
the medial prefrontcortex may have a role in integration and processing of feeding-related information in the rat.
the medial prefrontcortex is involved in the processing of the rewarding effects of liquid food.

we have shown for the first time the neuronal responses in the rat prefrontal cortex that are time locked to the onset of licking clusters.
